## How the live sessions work (on Zoom)

Our live sessions run in **breakout rooms**. You decide how you want to work:

::: {.vspace}
:::

::: {.vspace}
:::

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="31%"}
### Team up

* Work through the exercises in **teams of two or three**
* Come alone but want a partner? Tell us (see next slide) and we will match you with others
* Tip: one person shares their screen and codes, the others think along. Swap roles per exercise
:::

::: {.column width="3.5%"}
:::

::: {.column width="31%"}
### Solo, with help nearby

* Work on your own in the **shared help room**
* One of us is there most of the time
* Stuck? Just ask in the room or use Zoom's **Ask for help** button
:::

::: {.column width="3.5%"}
:::

::: {.column width="31%"}
### Do your own thing

* Explore your own data, a different model, or the material at your own pace
* You can leave the meeting if you want to
* Just come back to the main room when the breakout session ends
* You can reach us any time via the chat or by joining the help room
:::

::::


## How to join

1. We open a **poll**: choose *Team up*, *Solo*, or *Own thing*
2. **Looking for a partner?** Choose *Team up* and join the room "Looking for a partner". We will form groups of two to three there and send you off to your own room
3. Otherwise, pick a room yourself from the breakout room list:
    * **Teams**: your own room, once you are matched
    * **Help desk**: the shared help room
4. You can switch rooms at any point. Teams can also split up or merge

**We will announce when the breakout session is about to end. Please come back to the main room then.**

* Stuck on an exercise? Prefitted models and the solution scripts are in the `live_session` directory


--- 



## Get to the Material


### Get the workshop materials from our workshop Github:

#### With package `usethis` (recommended, no Git or GitHub account needed)

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

install.packages("usethis")
usethis::use_course("KennethKoslowski/mlts_workshop_EAM_2026")
```

* This downloads the workshop directory as a ZIP file, unpacks it into a folder of your choice, and (usually) opens the R project in a new R session
* If no new R session opens, open the file `mlts_workshop_EAM_2026.Rproj` in the new folder by clicking it


#### Or download the Github project as ZIP file:

1. Open the link: [https://github.com/KennethKoslowski/mlts_workshop_EAM_2026](https://github.com/KennethKoslowski/mlts_workshop_EAM_2026)
2. Click the green Code button, then Download ZIP
3. Extract the ZIP file
4. Open the `mlts_workshop_EAM_2026.Rproj` file by clicking it (it should open in a new R session)


---

## Things to Prepare for the Workshop

#### Quick overview of the workshop directory

The workshop directory from Github contains all the workshop materials.

* Follow the slides by opening `index.html` in the main directory in your browser
* The directory `live_session` contains scripts (and solutions) for the hands-on session exercises. You can directly work within the script or create them yourself!

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width = "45%"}

#### Required packages

* For following along all the examples by yourself, you need the current development version of `mlts`
* We prepared the R script `install_packages.R` in the directory `live_session`. Please run it once by opening it and running all lines of code or copy in the R console:

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

source("./live_session/install_packages.R")
```

* If you are asked to install updates, click yes to all. It might take a few minutes!

:::

::: {.column width = "5%"}
:::

::: {.column width = "45%"}
#### Data

* We use data from a study by @Bolzenkoetter2024 (openly available)
* To get the data locally, please run the script `bolzen_prepare.R` in the directory `live_session`:

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

source("./live_session/bolzen_prepare.R")
```

* This will generate data files in a directory called `downloaded_data`

:::
::::
